source_quote: Low-activity sedentary dog populations carried significantly higher overweight and obesity prevalence in wellness screening data.
Sedentary small companion dogs maintained high periodontal disease prevalence in primary-care veterinary populations.
Medium-activity dog profiles showed stable otitis externa prevalence across general practice surveillance data.
Atopic dermatitis prevalence remained moderate in medium-energy general practice canine populations.
High-energy working and sporting dog populations showed elevated cranial cruciate ligament rupture incidence.
High-energy working lineages carried increased exercise-induced collapse prevalence under strenuous field activity conditions.
Extreme-activity canine populations demonstrated the highest cruciate ligament rupture incidence across energy strata.
Extreme-energy dogs had increased heat-related illness events under warm environmental conditions.
High-drive athletic dogs showed elevated exertion-associated gastrointestinal disturbance prevalence in training populations.
High-energy working dogs developed moderate osteoarthritis prevalence with cumulative mechanical load and age.
